sections.h2: Which Warrenton offices deal with a property tax bill?
sections.html:
Both of them share one address on Main Street in Warrenton: 521 Main Street, ZIP 30828. One counter collects the money and the other decides what each parcel is worth, so the office you call depends on whether your problem is the amount or the payment.

The commissioner is an elected constitutional officer. The job runs from homestead paperwork and digest preparation through billing, bookkeeping and the hand-off to the school system and local governments. Real estate, utilities, vehicles, mobile homes and timber all pass through that counter, and staff will run a card over the phone if you would rather skip the trip.

The commissioner's page also lists the office's holiday closures for 2026, which include Thanksgiving, the day after, Christmas Eve, Christmas Day and New Year's Day 2027, so plan a payoff request around them.

Source: the commissioner and assessor pages on warrencountyga.com.

The assessors' page carries a notice that appraisal staff may visit a property to refresh their records, citing state code section 48-5-264.1. Visitors arrive in a county vehicle and leave a card at the door when nobody answers.

sections.h2: How does Warren County's housing market look to a seller?
sections.html:
Warren is a quiet rural county where homes are inexpensive and almost nothing new gets built. QuickFacts shows 5,269 people in its July 2025 estimate, compared with 5,834 in the 2010 count and 5,215 in 2020. The county chamber describes Warrenton, Camak and Norwood as the business-friendly towns.

  • Land: 284.36 square miles, which works out to roughly 18 residents for each square mile.
  • Housing stock: 2,687 units, and owners occupy 72.2% of them.
  • What a home is worth to its owner in the 2020 through 2024 survey: $67,100 at the midpoint.
  • Median rent in that survey: $690. Permits issued in 2025: zero.

When a house is worth that little, a few years of unpaid tax plus interest can swallow a large piece of the price. Pay attention to old balances early. The county's own site calls the area the gateway to rural Georgia and leans on farming, history and the outdoors.

More survey detail: 2,097 households of about 2.43 people each, 93.8% of residents in the same home a year earlier, 63.2% with broadband at home, and median household income of $44,289. Buyers who telecommute will want to check connectivity at the specific address.

sections.h2: When does a Warren County tax bill become late?
sections.html:
Georgia's default is December 20, though a county board can pull the date forward to December 1 or November 15 or use installments. The tax commissioner can tell you which schedule your bill follows. State guidance gives every owner 60 days after the postmark before interest starts.

Warren's economic development page explains that the city of Warrenton, Warren County itself, the school system and the state each levy tax as of January 1, and every parcel is assessed at 40% of market value. It prints 30.358 mills for 2017 and an effective rate of 1.21%, which is a historical figure. For a current rate, ask the commissioner about your parcel or read the county finance page, which says the commissioners publish a current digest and a five-year history of levy. That page also says tax hearings are advertised whenever a proposed millage rate exceeds the rollback rate, and it carries the 2026-2027 proposed and tentative budgets and an audit posted July 6, 2026.

  • Returns run January 1 to April 1. If you skip one, last year's value rolls forward.
  • A mobile home owner applies for a location permit within 30 days of placing the unit, then renews each year in the same window.
  • Overpayments can be reclaimed if the request starts within three years.

sections.h2: How can a Warren County owner challenge a value?
sections.html:
Put the appeal in writing and send it to the assessors' board, carrying a postmark within 45 days of the mailing date printed on your notice. State guidance lists taxability, value, uniformity and denied exemptions as acceptable reasons. Mail it to the county board rather than the state, which cannot take it.

Form PT-311A makes you choose a path. Most owners choose the equalization board route. A hearing officer only hears non-homestead real estate worth more than $500,000, and arbitration needs a certified appraisal that you supply.

Still unhappy? A written notice for superior court has to reach the county board within a month of the hearing officer's, arbitrator's or Board of Equalization's decision, and taxes must be paid at last year's level before a judge hears the case. If the final value ends at 85% or less of the earlier figure, the owner recovers litigation costs and attorney's fees.

sections.h2: What does the local economy mean for property values?
sections.html:
A thin job base keeps demand modest, and QuickFacts shows it. The county had 76 employer establishments in 2023 with 977 jobs, a 1.4% decline in employment from 2022, and 720 businesses with no employees. Annual payroll totaled $53.2 million, and retail sales for 2022 came to $13.27 million, or $2,573 per resident.

The Development Authority of Warren County tries to change that with incentives its page lists: low-cost land, tax abatement schedules, industrial revenue bond financing, a $4,000 job tax credit per new job for five years, and a 100% freeport exemption on inventory shipped out of state. The page notes that Warren is a Tier 1 community. These programs target businesses, but a seller with commercial or industrial land should ask the authority what applies.

Poverty is 24.6% in the Census estimate, and 12.3% of adults over 25 have finished a bachelor's degree. Those numbers help explain the price level. In a market with few buyers, an owner who arrives with a clear title and paid-up taxes has an easier path to closing.

sections.h2: Does Warren County add its own homestead exemption?
sections.html:
No. The state's revenue department shows no local exemption in Warren, so owners rely on the statewide ones. The form goes in at any point after the home becomes your primary residence, and it needs to arrive by April 1 for the first year you want relief. Missing that date forfeits the exemption for the year.

The commissioner's page says staff handle these applications. Carry proof that you live in the house and ask which age or disability categories you could add. A buyer who will live in the house files a new form of their own, which is worth mentioning when the closing falls late in the year.

sections.h2: How does a sale close out the Warren County tax bill?
sections.html:
The bill follows whoever owned the property on January 1, so sellers and buyers split it on the settlement statement. Ask the commissioner for a written balance that covers each year up to the closing date, then give that paper to the closing attorney. A house inside Warrenton, Camak or Norwood may owe a city levy on top of the county one.

  • Get separate figures for the county, the school district and any city.
  • Check whether a mobile home or timber account sits under the same name.
  • Keep your receipts for three years in case a refund claim comes up.

faqs.q: Who answers questions about a Warren County tax bill?
faqs.a: The tax commissioner does, at 706-465-2231. The office is at 521 Main Street in Warrenton, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 189, Warrenton, GA 30828. Value disputes go to the assessors at 706-465-3321.

faqs.q: By when must a Warren County value dispute be mailed?
faqs.a: Your envelope needs a postmark inside 45 days of the notice mailing date. Address it to the county's assessors in writing. State offices do not take these appeals.

faqs.q: Is there a Warren County exemption beyond the state homestead one?
faqs.a: No local exemption is listed for Warren County by the state revenue department. Owners use the statewide homestead exemptions and apply by April 1 for the first year.

faqs.q: What percentage of value does Warren County tax?
faqs.a: Property is assessed at 40% of fair market value, according to the county's economic development page. Exemptions come off that figure before the millage rate applies.

faqs.q: Can I give a card number over the phone to pay Warren County taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The commissioner's page says staff take card payments by phone, and it links an online option too. Call 706-465-2231 to ask about fees.
